nonBlocking: commandTimelineEnabled.didSet fires on redundant same-value sets (true->true) and, if a deferred segment is open, zeros the pending kernel/encode accumulators and marks the segment partial; the next flush then reports kernelCount/encodeSeconds nil. Conservative and documented for toggles, but a redundant set is also treated as a toggle. Consider guarding with oldValue != commandTimelineEnabled.

Gemma4CommandTimeline.Summary has no public initializer (synthesized memberwise init is internal). Decoding works, but external consumers cannot construct a Summary directly; fine for a derived type, worth stating in the doc comment.

The hardware probe gate asserts zero-tolerance containment gpuStart >= hostBeforeCommit and gpuEnd <= hostAfterWait on 3 blit buffers. The reasoning (GPUStartTime/GPUEndTime documented as host seconds, same mach_absolute_time basis as CACurrentMediaTime) is sound and the patch correctly treats a failure as information rather than a correctness regression, but this is the one assertion that cannot be judged without running; build/tests are pending.

When both breakdownInstrumentation and commandTimelineEnabled are on, the deferred-branch encode accumulation (one extra hostSeconds() call) lands inside the breakdown encode window because the breakdown defer runs after it. Negligible and only when both diagnostics are on; the off path for each remains a single Bool branch.

flushOpenSegment zeros ctPendingKernels/ctPendingEncodeSeconds/ctPendingPartial unconditionally (three stores) even when tracing is off. Harmless, consistent with the stated off-path cost, and keeps state coherent across toggles.

Documented, not fixed: JSONEncoder default strategy throws on NaN/inf in raw traces; per-kernel mode saturates the 8192-event bound within a few tokens (truncated/droppedCount must be checked); the probe records kernelCount nil because it uses a blit.
deviceProbe creates its own MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice; fine for a standalone clock-basis check, and it never touches a runner, as stated.
rationale: Scope matches the request: opt-in, bounded command-buffer timeline diagnostics at exactly the three existing commit/wait sites (flushOpenSegment, dispatch direct branch, dispatchPipeline direct branch) with no added flushes, completion handlers, readbacks, or command buffers. Kernels, SSA, segmentation, synchronization, quantization, the 1e-4 logit gate and the 32/31 exact gates are untouched; the applied Gemma4.swift shows every original statement (status guard, throw text, submittedBuffers, gpuMicrosTotal, kernelGpuMicrosByName, dispatchCountTotal, expertCache hooks) in original order. Off path: each site evaluates one Bool and the ternaries skip hostSeconds(); nothing is appended. Events are recorded after waitUntilCompleted and before the status guard, so failed buffers are captured with completed=false and still throw exactly as before; discardOpenSegment and beginSegment semantics are unchanged. Clock basis is handled correctly: host time is mach_absolute_time scaled by mach_timebase_info (the CACurrentMediaTime conversion), a failed timebase yields NaN so every event is rejected rather than mis-scaled, and the shared basis with GPUStartTime/GPUEndTime is verified per event by bounds containment rather than assumed. Analysis validates in the required order (sequence, completed, finite including encode, positive, host order, encode sign, GPU order, GPU inside host bounds, overlap with previous valid) before deriving any gap, never clamps, derives gaps only between adjacent valid sequence numbers, counts missing and skipped pairs, and surfaces truncation. The synthetic test timeline uses binary-exact values and the hand-checked totals (commit 0.75, wait 5.25, gpu 2.5, commitToGpuStart 2.0, gpuEndToWaitReturn 1.5, span 7.0, gap 1.5/0.5/1.0) and rejection reasons all agree with the code. The patch summary makes no performance or gain claim, explicitly preserves the failing 40.46%/23.81% A/A controls as unaddressed, states that gaps are host wall time rather than CPU busy time, does not equate flush-minus-GPU with CPU busy, and claims no process attribution. Replacement anchors are unique within Gemma4.swift (the two identical commit/wait blocks are disambiguated by their trailing comments). Build and tests have not been run; the only runtime-dependent assertion is the hardware probe containment check, flagged above.
